guitar.evidence: Jimi Hendrix's white Fender Stratocaster (played upside-down/restrung for a right-handed guitar as a left-handed player) is one of the most iconic guitar associations in rock history.

tone.target: nasal octavia fuzz with tight riff crunch
tone.profile: nasal octavia fuzz with tight riff crunch
tone.summary: The signal chain uses Fuzz/Red Haze for the core texture, followed by an OD boost (Green OD) to tighten the rhythm, running through a classic British amp model (UK 45) with minimal reverb and a wah filter applied dynamically.

rig.name: Jimi Hendrix - Crosstown Traffic - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain a tight edge.
Simulate the Octavia/Fuzz Face bite and raw fuzz texture.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze is used to capture the aggressive, nasal character of an octave fuzz without needing a dedicated octaver model.

blocks.purpose: Provide a tight, focused boost for the rhythm parts and upper mids.
blocks.gap: Used as a secondary drive/boost to maintain definition over the fuzz texture.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required nasal filter sweep (wah effect).
Simulate the punchy, classic British small amp sound (Plexi/Marshall).
blocks.gap: The UK 45 provides the necessary mid-focus and raw edge.

blocks.purpose: Provide a punchy and articulate British cabinet tone.
Enhance the bright upper mids and cut unnecessary low-end mud.
blocks.gap: Used for surgical tone shaping to achieve 'bright upper mids'.

blocks.purpose: Add minimal, natural room ambience without sounding lush or wet.
blocks.gap: The 'minimal reverb' requirement is met by keeping the mix very low.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for a more authentic, punchy British rock sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the raw, punchy edge required for classic Hendrix tone.
